name: Wild salmon
tile_uses: The weekend meal, the tomato plate, rice bowls
why_now: Wild Pacific salmon — king, sockeye, coho — is caught from late spring through summer, and July is when it's at its best and most available. Most of the year, salmon is farmed and the same every week. This is the month it's a seasonal fish.
how_to_choose: Deep, even color — sockeye is the reddest, king the richest
Moist and glossy, with no gaps between the layers
It should smell like the ocean, nothing else
A thicker center cut roasts more evenly than a tail piece
buy_this_much: 1½ lbs, in one piece. The weekend meal, plus a tomato plate or rice bowl for lunch.
price_note: Wild costs more than farmed. In July, the difference is worth it at least once.

flavor_paths.name: Slow-roasted
flavor_paths.description: 275°F, twenty minutes, until it just flakes. The weekend meal.

flavor_paths.name: Cool
flavor_paths.description: Flaked over cucumber yogurt with mint.

weekday_uses: Over a rice bowl with cucumber yogurt
Cold, the next day, with lime and flaky salt
weekend_use: Slow-roasted at 275°F, beside tomatoes and burrata. The weekend meal.
storage: Cook it the day you buy it, or the next. Leftovers keep two days in the fridge and are good cold.
one_thing_to_learn: Salmon is done earlier than you think. The white beads that rise to the surface are proteins being squeezed out; a few means it's perfect, a lot means it's dry. Low heat gives you time to see them.
market_question: Is this wild or farmed, and which kind?
